title: Hard-Coded Global Singleton (Global Access Path)
pattern: Domain functions or structs access globally shared mutable or connection state directly via global statics, static Singletons, or lazy-static definitions rather than receiving them as arguments.
why_bad: It tightly couples the codebase to a single global concretion. Testing methods in parallel becomes impossible due to shared state. Swapping the DB pool or mocking it for localized unit tests requires modifying all calling code.
detection: Explicit calls to global static references or static singletons directly inside private helper methods or domain logic functions.
counterexample: Truly immutable, global compile-time constants (such as physical constants or mathematical values) that bear zero operational volatility.
fix: Utilize dependency injection. Pass the database connection pool reference `&Pool` explicitly into the function signature, or supply it as a field during struct construction.
source: Erich Gamma et al., *Design Patterns* (1994), "Singleton"; Michael Feathers, *Working Effectively with Legacy Code* (2004), Chapter 9 ("The Case of the Irritating Global Dependency"), pp. 120-124.
